note: Original descriptions of each aspect in each position, written as observable behaviour. Keys are the aspect letter followed by the position number.

V1.summary: Knows what they want and acts on it without asking permission.
V1.behaviour: Decisions come quickly and stay made. They take charge as a matter of course, and other people's wishes are something to weigh, not something that sets the direction. They protect others readily, but on their own terms.
signs: Makes the call in a group without waiting to be asked
Rarely revisits a decision once it's made
Pushes back calmly when someone tries to decide for them

V2.behaviour: They can lead and enjoy having a say, but they treat decisions as something to work out with others. They'll give ground on how something is done while holding on to what matters to them, and they enjoy the back-and-forth of it.
signs: Enjoys negotiating and finding a deal both sides accept
Changes plans without feeling defeated
Leads when needed and steps back without fuss

V3.summary: Sensitive about being pushed around, and unsure of their own wants.
V3.behaviour: Pressure feels personal. They may give in and resent it later, or dig in hard over something small to prove they can't be controlled. Choosing for themselves can take a long time, and being told what to do stings more than they show.
signs: Agonises over decisions, then defends them fiercely
Reacts sharply to being ordered about
Avoids situations where they'd have to assert themselves openly

V4.behaviour: They don't need to be in charge and are comfortable following a clear lead. Being told what to do isn't an insult; it often comes as a relief. Their own wants tend to emerge through other people's plans rather than against them.
signs: Says "whatever you prefer" and means it
Works best with clear direction
Rarely fights over who gets their way

L1.summary: Holds firm views and states them as conclusions.
L1.behaviour: They've thought things through and present their opinions as settled. They explain readily and like to be the one who makes sense of things, but they aren't easily argued out of a view, and debate is for informing others more than for changing their own mind.
signs: Answers questions with a clear position, not a list of options
Explains how things work without being asked
Stays unmoved by arguments they've already considered

L2.summary: Enjoys thinking things through with other people.
L2.behaviour: Ideas are something to play with and test. They like discussion, can see several sides, and will happily update a view when a better argument comes along. Thinking is a process they enjoy, not a ruling they hand down.
signs: Likes a good debate for its own sake
Says "good point" and changes their mind
Explores a question before settling on an answer

L3.summary: Worries about looking foolish or being wrong.
L3.behaviour: They care about having the right answer and take intellectual criticism hard. They may avoid stating opinions where they could be challenged, defend a view rigidly once it's out, or lean on experts and rules to feel on solid ground.
signs: Holds back opinions in a group of confident talkers
Feels stung when their reasoning is picked apart
Checks with an authority before committing to a view

L4.summary: Relaxed about ideas and happy to borrow other people's.
L4.behaviour: They don't see themselves as a thinker and don't mind. Arguments and theories can bore them, and they readily adopt the view of someone they trust. They're more likely to go on instinct or experience than reason a thing out.
signs: Defers to someone who seems to know
Loses interest in long debates
Says "I don't really have a view on that" without discomfort

E1.summary: Expresses feelings fully and sets the emotional tone.
E1.behaviour: Their feelings are clear and strong, and they share them without hesitation. They lift or lower the mood of a room, and they give emotional support generously, though they don't easily take on other people's moods in return.
signs: Openly enthusiastic, moved or upset
Others pick up on their mood straight away
Comforts people readily but rarely asks for comfort

E2.summary: Emotionally responsive and in tune with others.
E2.behaviour: They feel things vividly and enjoy emotional exchange. They match and shape the mood around them, share feelings easily, and are open to other people's feelings changing theirs. Expressing emotion is something they do with others, not at them.
signs: Picks up and responds to others' moods
Enjoys heartfelt conversations
Laughs or tears up easily alongside others

E3.summary: Feels a lot but finds it hard to show.
E3.behaviour: Feelings run deep, but expressing them feels exposed and awkward. They may keep a cool or restrained surface, worry about being too much or too little, and feel hurt when their feelings are dismissed or mocked. Big displays of emotion around them can be uncomfortable.
signs: Looks composed while churning inside
Dislikes being asked how they feel in front of others
Remembers for a long time when their feelings were brushed aside

E4.summary: Calm and not much moved by mood.
E4.behaviour: They don't give feelings much importance, theirs or other people's, and aren't bothered by that. They can seem steady or unflappable, and they'll happily let someone more expressive bring the warmth. Emotional drama tends to pass them by.
signs: Stays level when others are worked up
Rarely talks about how they feel
Is content for others to supply the excitement

F1.summary: At home in the physical world and sure of their own comfort.
F1.behaviour: They know what they like in their surroundings, possessions and physical life, and they arrange things to suit. They handle practical and material matters confidently, look after other people's physical comfort and needs, and don't need advice on how to live.
signs: Has a settled way of keeping home, money and things
Takes care of practical matters for others
Isn't swayed by others' ideas of how they should live

F2.summary: Enjoys physical activity, comfort and the material world.
F2.behaviour: They like doing things with their hands and body and take pleasure in comfort, objects and surroundings. They adapt easily to new physical settings and enjoy sharing physical activities and comforts with others.
signs: Throws themselves into hands-on activities
Enjoys shopping, making or fixing things with others
Adapts quickly to a new place or routine

F3.summary: Anxious about the physical and material side of life.
F3.behaviour: Comfort, money, possessions or physical competence feel uncertain. They may worry about doing practical things badly, feel judged on their appearance or surroundings, or swing between neglecting these areas and fussing over them.
signs: Feels self-conscious doing practical tasks in front of others
Worries over money or possessions out of proportion
Is hurt by comments about their home, clothes or appearance

F4.summary: Undemanding about physical comfort and material things.
F4.behaviour: They don't pay much attention to their surroundings, possessions or comfort and are content to let others handle practical arrangements. They put up with discomfort without complaint and often lose track of the physical side of life while absorbed in something else.
signs: Doesn't notice or mind a messy or spare setting
Happily lets someone else organise practical matters
Forgets physical upkeep when busy
